bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42475442 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42475442
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source checkout / staged PoC bytes
bug_description.normalized: The exact 5-byte witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd` makes `fuzz_disasmnext` select platform index 14 and pass instruction bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into Capstone's PowerPC big-endian decoder. `getInstruction()` assembles those bytes into `insn == 0x7c2005dd`, and `DecoderTable32` classifies that word as `TSR` with decode recipe 71. Recipe 71 creates exactly one immediate operand in `MI->Operands[0]`. On this path the generated printer still keeps `TSR` in the `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)` arm, so it reads `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` even though slot 1 was never written. The memory-safety bug exists because `MCInst_Init()` only marks each operand slot `kInvalid` and does not initialize the union payload of untouched slots in the stack-allocated `mci` object. `printUInt32()` then consumes that indeterminate value in its `val > HEX_THRESHOLD` branch, and MemorySanitizer reports a use-of-uninitialized-value at `SStream.c:177`. The staged fix resolves the bug by zeroing every `Operands[i].ImmVal` in `MCInst_Init()` before any later wrong-slot read can occur.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the PowerPC instruction word that drives the vulnerable decode and print path.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is the exact 5-byte input `0e 7c 20 05 dd`. Byte `0x0e` makes `get_platform_entry()` select platform index 14 in `suite/fuzz/platform.c`, and bytes `7c 20 05 dd` are assembled here into `insn == 0x7c2005dd`.

root_cause.description: Scored root cause. `MCInst_Init()` marks each operand slot invalid but leaves the union payload of untouched slots undefined, so a later read from an unwritten slot observes leftover stack bytes from `cs_disasm`'s local `mci`. The fix adds `inst->Operands[i].ImmVal = 0;` in this loop.
root_cause.note: On the witness path, decode recipe 71 writes only `Operands[0]` while the generated `TSR` printer later asks for `Operands[1]`. Because this loop never defines `Operands[1].ImmVal`, the later immediate read is a use-before-init.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The uninitialized value loaded from `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` reaches `printUInt32()` as `val` and is consumed by this branch.
sink.note: The saved MSan stack is `printUInt32 -> printU1ImmOperand -> printInstruction -> cs_disasm`, which matches this sink exactly.

tainted_value_origin.description: Stack allocation of the `MCInst` whose untouched operand-union bytes later back `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal`. The saved MSan origin points to this `cs_disasm` stack frame; `MCInst_Init()` later clears kinds and size but, before the fix, does not define `ImmVal` for unwritten slots.

parser_admitted.description: With the selected PowerPC big-endian handle and no QPX/SPE mode bits, `getInstruction()` reaches `DecoderTable32`, which accepts `0x7c2005dd` as `TSR` instead of failing.

printer_called.description: After successful decode, `cs_disasm()` invokes the architecture printer on the partially populated `MCInst`, reaching the generated `TSR` printer case that requests operand slot 1.

evidence_limitations: The saved MSan report shows only the consumer stack and the `cs_disasm` origin frame; the exact `TSR` mnemonic is reconstructed statically from the witness word `0x7c2005dd` and the generated `DecoderTable32` filters in the staged source.

The saved stack does not expose inlined `MCInst_getOperand` or `MCOperand_getImm` helper frames, so the invalid-slot immediate read is reconstructed from the composite expression in `printU1ImmOperand()` plus the helper implementations in `MCInst.c`.

coarse_trace.summary: The first witness byte `0x0e` makes the fuzz harness select platform index 14, open the PowerPC big-endian backend, and pass the remaining bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `cs_disasm()`.
Capstone reuses stack `MCInst mci` for each decode. `MCInst_Init()` resets operand kinds and size but, in the vulnerable code, leaves the `ImmVal` union bytes of unused slots untouched.
The PowerPC parser assembles witness bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `0x7c2005dd`, matches that word to `TSR`, and recipe 71 appends only one immediate operand at slot 0.
The generated `TSR` printer still requests operand slot 1, so `printU1ImmOperand()` reads `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal` even though the decoder initialized only slot 0.
The uninitialized slot-1 value is forwarded to `printUInt32()` and consumed by the `val > HEX_THRESHOLD` branch, producing the saved MemorySanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: The witness selector byte `0x0e` maps to platform index 14, so the harness opens the PowerPC big-endian backend and passes the remaining attacker-controlled bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `cs_disasm()`.

Root cause. This loop invalidates each operand slot but does not define the union payload for unwritten slots. On the stack-allocated `mci` object from `cs_disasm`, `Operands[1].ImmVal` therefore remains indeterminate unless a later decode step overwrites it.
Source. For the witness, the big-endian branch is taken and attacker-controlled bytes `7c 20 05 dd` become `insn == 0x7c2005dd`.
The generated decoder state machine classifies `0x7c2005dd` as `TSR`: `DecoderTable32` follows the `bits[1:0] == 1` and `bits[10:6] == 23` branch to `MCD_OPC_Decode, 184, 12, 71 // Opcode: TSR`.
Decode recipe 71 extracts bit 21 (`tmp == 1`) and appends it as the only explicit operand. After this step, `MI->size == 1`, `MI->Operands[0].ImmVal == 1`, and `MI->Operands[1]` is still untouched.

fine_trace.code:
// TBEGIN, TEND, TSR, XSRQPI, XSRQPIX, XSRQPXP
printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O);
fine_trace.note: The vulnerable generated printer still keeps `TSR` in case 18 and asks `printU1ImmOperand()` for operand slot 1 even though step 4 populated only slot 0 and left `MI->size == 1`. There is no `MCInst_getNumOperands(MI) > 1` guard before slot 1 is used.

With `OpNo == 1`, `MCInst_getOperand()` returns `&MI->Operands[1]` and `MCOperand_getImm()` reads that slot's `ImmVal` without a bounds or kind check. Because step 4 never wrote slot 1 and step 1 never initialized `ImmVal` for untouched slots, this expression loads the uninitialized stack contents of `MI->Operands[1].ImmVal`.
The uninitialized operand value is forwarded unchanged to the generic unsigned printer.
Sink. `printU1ImmOperand()` passes the uninitialized `Value` into `printUInt32()`, and this branch is the first observed use that MemorySanitizer reports.

allocation_context.description: Saved MSan origin: the uninitialized value was created by stack allocation of `mci` in the `cs_disasm` frame. The declaration itself is `MCInst mci;` at line 796.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MSan report names `printUInt32` at `SStream.c:177:6`, which is the exact fine-trace sink.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The saved origin is the stack `mci` object in `cs_disasm`, and the scored root cause is the immediately related partial initializer in `MCInst_Init()` that fails to define `Operands[i].ImmVal` for untouched slots of that same object.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `printUInt32 -> printU1ImmOperand -> printInstruction -> cs_disasm`; the fine trace fills in the PowerPC big-endian `getInstruction()` branch, the `TSR` decoder selection, recipe 71's single operand creation, and the untouched slot-1 state between `cs_disasm` and the printer call.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. `printInstruction` passes `OpNo = 1`, `printU1ImmOperand` fetches `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)->ImmVal`, and `printUInt32` immediately branches on that poisoned `Value`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix adds `inst->Operands[i].ImmVal = 0;` to `MCInst_Init()`'s initialization loop. With that change, unwritten operand slots such as `MI->Operands[1]` become defined before the later `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)` read, so the saved MSan use-of-uninitialized-value no longer occurs.

poc.trigger: Exact 5-byte witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd`. Byte `0x0e` selects platform index 14 in the fuzz harness, and bytes `7c 20 05 dd` decode as the vulnerable PowerPC `TSR` path until MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `printUInt32`.

format.name: libFuzzer input: 1-byte platform selector + 4-byte PPC instruction
format.contract: Use the exact 5-byte witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd`. The first byte must remain `0x0e` so `get_platform_entry()` selects platform index 14 and opens the PowerPC big-endian backend; the remaining four bytes must remain `7c 20 05 dd` so `getInstruction()` materializes `0x7c2005dd`, `DecoderTable32` selects `TSR` recipe 71, and the generated printer later reads unwritten operand slot 1. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact selector/instruction pair.
